groups.name: core-integrity
groups.label: Core integrity (Open Core + Pro boundary)
groups.purpose: Verifies the MIT Core contains no Pro code and every route is classified correctly

groups.name: security-environment
groups.label: Security and environment
groups.purpose: Validates the environment, secrets and deployment configuration are secure

groups.name: workflow-pipeline
groups.label: CI/CD pipeline
groups.purpose: Validates all GitHub Actions workflows are correct and secure (check:workflows owns the security and documented-vars steps)

groups.name: quality-code
groups.label: Code quality
groups.purpose: Type-checking, bounded linting, chunk limits and the esbuild/RxDB guards

groups.name: content-integrity
groups.label: Content integrity and i18n
groups.purpose: Verifies all visible content is in sync with the code and properly localized

groups.name: brand-visual
groups.label: Brand and visual elements
groups.purpose: Verifies brand consistency (logo, static tokens, sitemap) plus SEO, CSP and visual tokens

groups.name: security-depth
groups.label: Deep security
groups.purpose: Full security chain (CVE, CSP, legal), audit drift, licenses and Pro-history boundaries

groups.name: build-verification
groups.label: Build verification
groups.purpose: Visual-drift and gate-reachability checks plus the production build; the browser performance gate (check:performance) runs in the CI build job, where its report is generated against the same dist/

usage.ci:local: npm run ci:local = typecheck:prod + typecheck:server + lint + test:fast + build:ci + full check
usage.ci:groups: Run individual groups to iterate faster; every group command is an npm alias and is validated before it runs
usage.example: # Only verify Core integrity and security instead of the full chain
usage.command: npm run check:ci-groups core-integrity && npm run check:ci-groups security-environment
